newsitem.title: USA: NCAA AMERICAN FOOTBALL- NAVY TOPS CALIFORNIA IN ALOHA BOWL SHOOTOUT.
newsitem.headline: NCAA AMERICAN FOOTBALL- NAVY TOPS CALIFORNIA IN ALOHA BOWL SHOOTOUT.

text.p: Navy recorded its first post-season victory in 18 years on Wednesday as quarterback Ben Fay ran for a pair of fourth-quarter touchdowns to carry the Midshipmen to a wild 42-38 triumph over California in the Aloha Bowl.

Fay, who replaced Chris McCoy in the second half, went in from the 2-yard line with 7:39 remaining to bring Navy (9-3) within 38-35. His 10-yard dash with 1:41 left proved to be the winning touchdown.
California (6-6) had driven deep into Navy territory, but quarterback Pat Barnes fumbled away the ball on a third-down scramble at the 16 with three minutes remaining.

Fay then took Navy 84 yards in 89 seconds for the go-ahead score. He hit Ross Scott for a 15-yard gain on 3rd-and-8 to the Navy 33, then connected with Cory Schemm for a 51-yard gain to the Bears 15. Two plays later, Fay rolled left, cut inside and scored.

California got the ball back. But in one of the few displays of clutch defence, Barnes was sacked twice and the Midshipmen held on for their first post-season win since defeating Brigham Young, 23-16, in the 1978 Holiday Bowl.

The schools combined for 63 points in a wild see-saw first half, which started when California's Deltha O'Neal returned the opening kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown. O'Neal also had a 31-yard touchdown run in the second quarter.
McCoy ran for two of Navy's four first-half scores. Barnes threw three touchdown passes in the first half for California, which led 35-28 at halftime.
